title: Adaptive Higher-Order Intervals for Window-Restricted Dose Intervention Means
banked_reason: The delivered result is a feasible diagonal-histogram implementation theorem with matching window-target minimax risk, confined to the specified smoothness configuration and deterministic grid.
gap_reasons: The delivered result is a feasible diagonal-histogram implementation theorem with matching window-target minimax risk, confined to the specified smoothness configuration and deterministic grid.

The covariate-independent lower pair establishes the effective-window risk floor, while the zero-cell proposition establishes failure only of raw direct inversion and supplies no comparison against regularized localized alternatives.
proof_attempt_summary: The initial point-dose adaptation angle failed identification and validity review; the revised window-intervention angle established an observable diagonal weighted-Gram certificate, matching effective-window risk bounds, and an optimized histogram rank certificate. Mathematical review cleared the final derivation, but the general referee judged its contribution to be a specialized implementation of known decomposition and Gram-error ideas and capped its paper score below the field threshold. Reusing evaluation covariates for cell masses would require a new estimator and dependence theorem, so this run was banked at the achieved incremental tier.
tldr: The causal target is the window-restricted intervention mean \(\Psi_h(Q)\), identified by \(\tau_{P,h}\). A common outcome histogram and a deterministic bandwidth-indexed treatment-density family have uniform errors \(\varepsilon_{\mu,N}=(\log N/N)^{3/22}\) and \(\varepsilon_{\pi,N}(h)=(\log N/N)^{2/13}+m_{\pi,N}(h)^{-1/4}\). All reference-block covariates estimate positive weighted cell masses. On \(\mathcal H_N^\sharp=\{2^{-r}:N^{-2/5}/2<h\le N^{-30/143}(\log N)^{-1}\}\), this observable Gram permits \(Nh/16<k_N(h)\le Nh\), up to \(k_N(h)\asymp N^{113/143}(\log N)^{-1}\), with risk \(O\{(Nh)^{-1}\}\) and feasible-oracle discrepancy \(o\{(Nh)^{-1}\}\). The integrated-window lower pair gives the matching same-class risk order; raw unregularized dose-window inversion has the proved zero-cell obstruction. The sharper endpoint follows from the constrained pilot powers \(3/22\) and \(2/13\) and the independent-mass fluctuation power \(\sqrt h\).
gap: Localized higher-order risk theorems either use a fixed population projection kernel or leave feasible empirical-Gram error as a high-level operator-norm remainder. They do not certify an observable Gram at \(k\asymp Nh\) and do not pair that implementation result with a minimax frontier for the corresponding integrated stochastic-intervention mean.
fill: The project identifies \(\tau_{P,h}\) as \(\Psi_h(Q)\) by absolute continuity of the window intervention, derives a finite-sample simultaneous relative-mass theorem, and proves that \(\widehat\Pi_h\) replaces \(\Pi_{P,h}\) in Bonvini--Kennedy's separately trained histogram projection step with risk \(O\{(Nh)^{-1}\}\) and second-order Gram discrepancy. An explicit integrated-window pair proves the matching lower bound, and the raw localized diagonal is compared only through its proved zero-cell singularity.
